title: ToolRuntime Boundary
summary: Defines ToolRuntime as the governed tool execution authority. Ownership, capability boundaries, layered execution model, and separation from Ralph, desktop HITL, and analytics compiler.

sections.content: Rig Relay separates concerns between AgentLoop (turn conductor), ToolRuntime (governed execution authority), Ralph (observe-only scanner), the desktop HITL boundary, and the analytics compiler. ToolRuntime owns the governed tool execution path.

Desktop UI       Renders projections, sends intents. Dumb renderer.
Desktop Backend  Validates state, processes intents. Owns refusal codes.
Ralph            Scans projections, ranks candidates. Not an executor.
AgentLoop        Turn conductor — topology, middleware, session lifecycle.
ToolRuntime      Governed execution authority. Normalization, permission,
                 cache, gating, execution, receipt, refusal.
Analytics        Reads ledgers, compiles facts/projections. Never executes.

items: Patch proposal gating for mutation tools

sections.content: Ralph owns projection scanning, candidate ranking, mission candidate proposal, approval state and decision receipts. Ralph may submit bounded read-only missions to ToolRuntime through the desktop HITL boundary. Ralph must never execute tools directly, bypass permission gates, or mutate the workspace.
Desktop HITL Does Not Execute Tools
The desktop HITL boundary approves or declines mission candidates. Approval is a state transition, not an action trigger. Execution requires a separate contract through ToolRuntime.

RuntimeToolExecutionRunner → validate envelope → lease check →
ToolRuntime.execute_one() → governed tool invocation →
ToolRuntimeResult → runtime audit event
